name: Speed (distance ÷ time)
description: Computes average speed as distance÷time, in km/h from distance in km and time in hours. It is the constant speed that would cover the distance in the given time.
notes: This gives average speed, not instantaneous speed. Keep units matched (km and hours give km/h); convert minutes to hours before entering.

name: Fuel economy
description: Computes fuel economy as distance÷fuel, giving the distance travelled per litre of fuel in km/L. A higher value means better efficiency.
notes: This is km per litre, which is the inverse of L/100km used in some regions; a higher number is better here. Fuel must be nonzero.

name: Split the bill
description: Divides a total amount equally among a number of people, computing total÷people. The result is each person's equal share.
notes: This splits the total evenly; it does not handle unequal shares or added tips. The number of people must be nonzero.

name: Wage (rate × hours)
description: Computes gross pay as hourly rate×hours worked. The result is the total earnings before any deductions such as tax.
notes: This is gross pay, before tax or other deductions, and does not include overtime premiums unless those hours are entered separately.

name: Percentage of a number
description: Computes a given percentage of a number, using number×percent/100. For example 20 percent of 150 gives 30.
notes: Enter the percentage as a plain number (e.g. 20 for 20%), not as a fraction. The result is in the same unit as the input number.

name: Price before tax
description: Recovers the pre-tax price from a tax-included total by dividing the total by (1 + rate/100). It isolates the base amount before the given tax rate was added.
notes: Enter the tax rate as a percentage (e.g. 10 for 10%). This is not the same as simply subtracting the rate from the total, which overstates the deduction.

name: Total with tip and tax
description: Computes a final bill by applying tax and then tip multiplicatively to the base amount: bill × (1 + tax/100) × (1 + tip/100). Both rates are compounded onto the bill.
notes: Tip here is applied on the tax-inclusive amount because of the multiplication order. Enter tax and tip as percentages; applying tip on the pre-tax bill gives a lower total.

name: Stacked discount price
description: Applies two successive percentage discounts to a price: price × (1 − d1/100) × (1 − d2/100). The second discount is taken on the already-reduced amount.
notes: Stacked discounts do not add up; 20% then 10% is a 28% total reduction, not 30%. Enter each discount as a percentage.

name: Unit price
description: Calculates the price per single item by dividing the total price by the quantity. It lets you compare value across packs of different sizes.
notes: Both price and quantity must use consistent units; the result is cost per one unit. A lower unit price means better value for the same product.

name: Cost per serving
description: Divides the total cost by the number of servings to find how much each serving costs. Useful for budgeting recipes or meal planning.
notes: Servings must be a positive count; the result is cost per one serving. Include all ingredient costs in the total for an accurate figure.

name: Recipe scaling
description: Scales an ingredient amount for a new number of servings using amount × new servings / original servings. It keeps ingredient proportions the same as the original recipe.
notes: Assumes ingredients scale linearly, which is a good approximation but may not hold for seasonings, leavening, or cooking times.

name: Oven temp C to gas mark
description: Converts an oven temperature in Celsius to the British gas mark scale using (temp − 121) / 14. Higher gas marks correspond to hotter ovens.
notes: This is a linear approximation of the standard gas-mark table and may give fractional marks; round to the nearest whole mark in practice. Valid mainly within typical baking temperatures.

name: Paint needed
description: Estimates the liters of paint required as wall area ÷ coverage per liter × number of coats. It accounts for painting the surface multiple times.
notes: Coverage varies with surface porosity and paint type; the estimate ignores waste and touch-ups, so round up when buying.

name: Wall area (four walls)
description: Computes the combined area of the four walls of a rectangular room as 2 × (length + width) × height, i.e. the perimeter times the wall height.
notes: Does not subtract doors or windows, so it overestimates the paintable surface. Assumes a rectangular room with uniform wall height.

name: Room floor area
description: Calculates the floor area of a rectangular room by multiplying its length by its width.
notes: Valid only for rectangular floors; irregular shapes must be split into rectangles and summed. Both dimensions must share the same unit.

name: Tiles needed
description: Estimates how many tiles are needed by dividing floor area by the area of one tile, adding a waste margin, and rounding up to a whole number of tiles.
notes: Enter the waste margin as a percentage; the ceiling function ensures a whole tile count. Cuts, breakage, and pattern matching may require an even larger margin.

name: Wallpaper rolls
description: Estimates the number of wallpaper rolls needed by dividing total wall area by the area one roll covers and rounding up to a whole roll.
notes: Ignores pattern repeat and trimming waste, which can increase the count. The ceiling function rounds up so partial rolls become full rolls.

name: Concrete volume
description: Calculates the volume of a rectangular concrete slab or pour as length × width × depth, giving the amount of concrete in cubic meters.
notes: All three dimensions must be in meters to yield cubic meters. Order extra to allow for spillage, uneven subgrade, and formwork variation.

name: Mulch/soil volume
description: Computes the volume of mulch or soil for a bed as area × depth / 100, converting a depth given in centimeters and an area in square meters into cubic meters.
notes: Depth must be entered in centimeters; the division by 100 converts it to meters. Loose materials settle, so buy slightly more than the calculated volume.

name: Lawn seed needed
description: Calculates the grams of grass seed needed by multiplying the lawn area by the seeding rate per square meter.
notes: The seed rate depends on grass species and whether you are sowing new or overseeding. Area and rate must use the same area unit (square meters).

name: BTU for room cooling
description: Estimates the cooling capacity in BTU needed for a room by multiplying its floor area by a BTU-per-square-meter factor.
notes: The factor is a rough rule of thumb; sunlight, ceiling height, occupancy, and insulation all change the real requirement. Use it only for initial sizing.

name: Air changes per hour
description: Calculates how many times a room's air is fully replaced each hour as airflow × 60 / room volume, using airflow in cubic meters per minute.
notes: Airflow must be in m3/min (the ×60 converts to per hour) and volume in m3. Higher air changes per hour mean better ventilation.

name: Aspect-scaled width
description: Finds the new width that preserves the original aspect ratio for a given new height, using new height × original width / original height.
notes: Keeps the image proportions unchanged so it is not distorted. Round to whole pixels as needed; the same ratio logic applies when scaling by width instead.

name: Aspect ratio height
description: Computes the height that matches a target aspect ratio for a given width, using width × ratio height / ratio width (for example 16:9).
notes: Ratio height and width are the ratio terms (e.g. 9 and 16), not pixel sizes. Result may need rounding to whole pixels.

name: Photo print scaling
description: Scales a photo or print dimension by a percentage using original size × scale / 100. A scale over 100 enlarges and under 100 shrinks the size.
notes: Enter the scale as a percentage (150 means 150%). Apply the same scale to both width and height to keep proportions.

name: Currency with fee
description: Converts a foreign-currency amount into local currency and deducts a percentage fee, using amount × rate × (1 − fee/100). It gives the net amount received after conversion charges.
notes: Enter the fee as a percentage of the converted value. Real providers may add fixed charges or a spread in the rate, so the actual amount can be lower.

name: Hourly to annual salary
description: Estimates an annual salary from an hourly wage as rate × hours per week × 52 weeks in a year.
notes: Assumes 52 paid weeks with no unpaid time off; holidays, sick leave, and taxes are not deducted. It is a gross, pre-tax figure.

name: Annual to hourly rate
description: Converts an annual salary to an equivalent hourly rate by dividing it by hours per week × 52 weeks.
notes: Uses 52 weeks of work per year and does not account for paid leave or taxes. The result is a gross hourly figure before deductions.

name: Overtime pay
description: Calculates overtime pay as the hourly rate multiplied by a 1.25 premium and by the number of overtime hours worked.
notes: Assumes a 25% overtime premium; actual multipliers vary by law and contract (e.g. 1.35 for late-night or holiday work in Japan). Adjust the factor accordingly.

name: Net pay after tax
description: Computes take-home pay from gross pay by subtracting a deduction percentage, using gross × (1 − tax/100).
notes: Enter the combined deduction rate as a percentage. Real payroll uses progressive brackets and separate items (tax, pension, insurance), so a single flat rate is an approximation.

name: Monthly savings for goal
description: Determines how much to save each month to reach a target amount, by dividing the savings goal by the number of months available.
notes: Assumes equal monthly deposits and ignores any interest earned. If the savings earn interest, the required monthly amount would be somewhat lower.

name: Tip per person
description: Calculates each person's share of the tip by taking the tip percentage of the bill and dividing it among the people, using bill × tip/100 / people.
notes: This splits only the tip, not the bill itself; enter the tip as a percentage. Assumes the tip is shared equally among all people.

name: Cooking time by weight
description: Estimates total cooking time by multiplying the minutes required per kilogram by the weight of the food.
notes: The per-kilogram rate depends on the dish, oven, and doneness desired. Use a thermometer to confirm safe internal temperature rather than relying on time alone.

name: Calories from macros
description: Estimates total food energy from macronutrients using 4 kcal per gram of carbohydrate, 4 per gram of protein, and 9 per gram of fat.
notes: Uses standard Atwood energy factors; alcohol (about 7 kcal/g) and fiber are not included. Real values vary slightly by food.

name: Pace to speed
description: Converts a running pace in minutes per kilometer into speed in kilometers per hour by dividing 60 by the pace.
notes: Pace must be entered as minutes per kilometer in decimal form (6.5, not 6:30). Pace and speed are inversely related, so a faster pace gives a higher speed.

name: Speed to pace
description: Converts a speed in kilometers per hour into a running pace in minutes per kilometer by dividing 60 by the speed.
notes: The result is a decimal number of minutes; 6.5 means 6 minutes 30 seconds, not 6 minutes 50 seconds. Speed and pace are inversely related.

name: Travel time
description: Calculates how long a journey takes by dividing the distance by the average speed, giving travel time in hours.
notes: Assumes a constant speed and no stops; distance and speed must use consistent units (km and km/h). The decimal result is in hours, not hours and minutes.

name: Meeting cost
description: Estimates the labor cost of a meeting as the number of participants × each person's hourly cost × the meeting duration in hours.
notes: Assumes every participant shares the same hourly cost; use a blended average if rates differ. Captures only staff time, not overhead or opportunity cost.

name: Electricity cost
description: Calculates the cost of electricity by multiplying the energy consumed in kilowatt-hours by the unit price per kilowatt-hour.
notes: Uses a single flat unit price and excludes fixed base charges, fuel adjustments, and tiered rates that appear on real bills.

name: Water bill
description: Estimates a water bill as the volume used in cubic meters × the unit price, plus a fixed base charge.
notes: Assumes a single flat volumetric rate; many utilities use tiered pricing and add sewage charges separately. Base charge is added once.

name: Mortgage affordability
description: Gives a rough borrowing limit by multiplying annual income by an income multiple, a common rule of thumb for how large a mortgage might be affordable.
notes: This is only a screening heuristic; actual approval depends on interest rates, existing debts, deposit, and lender criteria. The multiple varies by market.

name: Rent rule of thumb
description: Applies the common guideline that rent should not exceed about 30% of income, returning 30% of monthly income as a suggested rent ceiling.
notes: This is a general benchmark, not a strict limit; affordable rent depends on other expenses, debts, and local costs. Some guidelines use gross and others net income.

name: Diagonal screen size
description: Computes the diagonal length of a rectangular screen from its width and height using the Pythagorean theorem, √(width² + height²).
notes: Width and height must share the same unit, and the result is in that unit. Screen sizes are often quoted in inches, so convert if your inputs are in centimeters.

name: Body fat mass
description: Estimates the mass of fat in the body by multiplying total body weight by the body-fat percentage. The result is the weight of fat tissue in kilograms, with the remainder being lean mass.
notes: Body fat must be entered as a percent value (20 for 20%), not a fraction. The percentage itself comes from a separate measurement such as calipers or a bioimpedance scale and carries its own error.

name: Miles to kilometers
description: Converts a distance in miles to kilometers by multiplying by the fixed factor 1.60934. The result is the same distance expressed in kilometers.
notes: The factor is for statute (land) miles, not nautical miles, which are about 1.852 km each. Conversion is exact and linear, so it works for any positive distance.

name: Split cost evenly
description: Divides a total amount by the number of people to give each person's equal share of the bill. The result is the amount one person pays when the cost is split evenly.
notes: The result is rounded to whole units, so rounding may leave the sum of shares slightly above or below the true total. People must be a positive count.

name: Coffee-to-water ratio
description: Divides the amount of water by the water-to-coffee ratio to find how many grams of ground coffee to use. A higher ratio means more water per gram of coffee and a weaker brew.
notes: The ratio is dimensionless (water grams per coffee gram); a value of 16 means 16 g water to 1 g coffee. Water is entered by weight in grams, where 1 g water is about 1 mL.

name: Compound interest total
description: Computes the future value of a principal that grows by a fixed annual rate compounded once per year over a number of years. The result is the total balance including accumulated interest.
notes: The rate is entered as a percent (3 for 3%) and compounding is assumed annual; more frequent compounding gives a larger total. It ignores deposits, withdrawals, taxes, and fees.
